CHIEF COMPLAINT: Exertional chest pressure for 3 weeks.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 63-year-old woman with hypertension and hyperlipidemia reports chest pressure walking uphill, relieved by rest. Recent stress echo showed a mild apical wall motion abnormality.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. Hypothyroidism.

FAMILY HISTORY: Father had coronary artery disease, MI at age 58. Mother with breast cancer.

MEDICATIONS: Lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.

ALLERGIES: NKDA.

VITALS: BP 152/90, HR 78.

ASSESSMENT: Stable angina, suspected coronary artery disease. Refer to cardiology for catheterization.
